title: Set authority and release contract
risk: Unauthorized activity or an unbounded gate
inputs: Commission, owner decisions, repository instructions, release purpose
method: Record whether this run permits reading, fixture tests, edits, local commits, private backup transfer, push, deployment and publication separately. Set one accountable worker, cost/time ceiling, target ref, supported claims and approval authority. Record requested versus independently observed model/effort/tier; UNKNOWN is allowed only if the owner permits it.
evidence: Signed-off scope record and capability/authority matrix
pass_criteria: No ambiguous mutation or external destination; required settings satisfied or explicit owner exception linked
limits: Owner decisions remain mandatory; the present research run authorizes no product execution or edits.

title: Identify baseline and all work
risk: Losing dirty work or qualifying the wrong source
inputs: Authorized repository, candidate branch, prior checkpoint
method: Read repository instructions and current checkpoint. Record canonical absolute path, worktree/branch ownership, base/head/tree identities, submodules/LFS where used, staged/unstaged/untracked paths and generated inputs. Reconcile concurrent writers before changes. Record baseline checks and pre-existing failures separately.
evidence: Identity receipt, redacted work inventory, command catalog with source locations
pass_criteria: Every intended change attributable; foreign work preserved; unresolved identity is a blocker
limits: Do not infer a clean tree from remote main or an old checkpoint.

title: Preserve private work and verify recovery
risk: Session loss or accidental source/secret publication
inputs: G01 inventory, approved local backup roots and recipients
method: Make a reversible private source checkpoint before edits and at every session end. Include intended untracked source and a manifest; list excluded credentials/operational state with protected-location references. Preserve the exact dirty patch plus base identity or a private local commit if authorized. Use access controls and encryption where required. Read back hashes and restore a small source fixture in a separate directory. External backup needs an approved private destination and transfer authority.
evidence: Checkpoint ID, inventory/hashes, exclusions and restore receipt
pass_criteria: Every unfinished source file is recoverable; private credentials remain protected; failed transfer is explicit LOCAL_ONLY
basis: S01 PS.3.1; S15; S22; engineering judgment
limits: A Git bundle alone misses uncommitted/untracked files. A local checkpoint is not disaster recovery or release approval.

title: Freeze a risk based check plan
risk: Checklist expansion or tests unrelated to real boundaries
inputs: Change diff, architecture, user workflows, prior evidence
method: List assets, actors, entry points, write paths, trust boundaries, supported platforms, storage states and optional dependencies. Select core and profiles. Create checks with fixed expected results, fixtures, budgets and stop criteria before execution. Classify APPLICABLE, NOT_APPLICABLE or UNDETERMINED with evidence. Reuse prior results only through an explicit unchanged-input argument. Plan bounded review for high-impact changes.
evidence: Threat sketch, applicability register, check-plan revision and prior-evidence reuse decisions
pass_criteria: All advertised critical paths and changed trust/data boundaries covered; unknown required scope becomes BLOCKED
limits: Add a new gate only for a release-relevant supported risk; log why and retire superseded checks.

title: Simplify without changing the contract
risk: Dead logic hides defects while cleanup introduces regressions
inputs: G01 baseline, G03 behavior invariants, authorized edit scope
method: Defluff means remove proven unused imports/dependencies, dead branches, redundant wrappers and comments that merely restate code. Inspect dynamic loading, reflection, platform conditions and external consumers before deletion. Keep small separate diffs. Characterize high-risk behavior before refactoring; compare outputs, errors, side effects and retained record digests. Defer architectural redesign or speculative optimization.
evidence: Cleanup ledger with removal rationale, focused equivalence results and reviewed diff
pass_criteria: Observable behavior and compatibility unchanged within documented inputs; uncertainty means retain or defer
limits: Line-count reduction and coverage reports alone cannot prove equivalence. Never remove defensive checks merely as clutter.

title: Resolve rights and preserve provenance
risk: Redistribution without notices or fabricated ownership
inputs: Exact included files/assets, upstream provenance, current license and owner evidence
method: Inventory project, copied/adapted, vendored, generated, fonts/images/docs and bundled-runtime materials. Record origin, pin, license, modifications, required notices and evidence of rights. Preserve upstream/historical notices. Confirm legal rights-holder spelling before changing project copyright. Apply reviewed SPDX-style metadata only where justified; use sidecars or REUSE.toml for non-commentable/generated paths, respecting shebangs and generated-file tooling.
evidence: File/provenance ledger, notice matrix, distributable license texts and unresolved ownership list
pass_criteria: No omitted known required notice or unlicensed included material; unresolved material removed from scope or rights resolved; optional header standard tracked separately
cost: 30–90 min; unresolved rights may need owner time
limits: MIT does not mandate an on-screen footer or universal per-file header. Full REUSE adoption is optional unless claimed.

title: Update brand without breaking compatibility
inputs: Approved current name and legal ledger
method: Classify references as product-facing current branding, legacy owned line, historical attribution, upstream notice or compatibility identifier. Change only approved current branding. Review CLI flags, environment variables, URLs, service names, config/data directories, package IDs and updater comparisons as interfaces. Provide aliases/migration where renamed. Regenerate derived assets only after source decisions.
evidence: Brand reference decisions, compatibility mapping and affected path tests
pass_criteria: Current product uses approved ARGELLAN identity; historical rights preserved; existing supported installations still discover data/config
limits: Bulk search-and-replace is unsafe. A new public number below 1.2.0 can be treated as a downgrade.

title: Run deterministic quality and build checks
risk: Syntax/style defects or unreproducible dependency resolution
inputs: Actual repository scripts/configuration and pinned toolchain
method: Extract commands from actual scripts, manifests and CI; record working directory, flags, side effects and authority. Use frozen dependency installation when a lockfile exists; inspect lifecycle scripts and dynamic downloads before execution. Run formatter in check mode, configured lint/types/syntax, and build. If missing, record NOT_CONFIGURED and use a scoped substitute with justification; do not invent npm scripts or install a toolchain silently.
evidence: Tool/version receipt, command/config citations, logs and dependency inventory
pass_criteria: Required configured checks pass with no unexplained warnings; exact dependency/runtime inputs known; missing required capability is BLOCKED
limits: Repeatable installation is weaker than bit-for-bit reproducible builds. No npm manifest exists at inspected CodexControl root.

title: Prove critical workflows and recovery paths
risk: Happy-path tests miss install, upgrade or user regressions
inputs: Frozen changed source, fixtures, support and compatibility contract
method: Run unit, integration and targeted historical regressions, including invalid inputs and failure states. Exercise fresh install and normal stop/start from the built candidate in a new private instance. Test supported upgrade and uninstall; downgrade only if promised, otherwise safe refusal plus documented restore. Verify browser/OS/architecture cells by actual environment. Check keyboard access, reduced motion and narrow screens for affected UI.
evidence: Results with pass/fail/skip counts, candidate hash and platform matrix
pass_criteria: All mandatory advertised cells pass; skips have reasons; removed support requires owner-approved documentation change
limits: A process listening or doctor PASS is not a working signed-in user workflow. Browser automation WebKit is not actual Safari qualification.

title: Measure performance against agreed budgets
risk: User-visible regressions, overload or misleading optimization claims
inputs: Representative workload, comparable baseline, host/browser instruments
method: Set workload and acceptance limits before measuring. Record raw runs, warm/cold state, hardware/runtime/browser, duration and concurrency. Measure startup, idle/active CPU/RSS, event-loop delay, ingest latency, browser frame/update work, network bytes, disk/backlog growth and export/replay. Use matched baseline/candidate fixtures and preserve record/provenance digests. Optimize only a measured issue; rerun equivalence and affected tests.
evidence: Raw timing/resource series, summary with variance/outliers and data equivalence receipt
pass_criteria: Owner-approved limits met under declared load; no silent data shedding or persistent growth beyond bound
cost: 45–90 min; longer soak only when justified
limits: Proposed first-run budget: three paired samples plus a 30-minute bounded soak; numbers in report are proposals, not product guarantees.

title: Perform a bounded security assessment
risk: Unreviewed trust boundary or false confidence from scanners
inputs: G03 threat map, exact candidate, explicit static/dynamic authorization
method: Use SEC01–SEC12 only where applicable. Pair control inspection with permitted success and rejection cases. Record static reasoning separately from execution, tool coverage, preconditions, source-to-sink trace, fixtures and observed response/state. Scan only when authorized and approved for private-code handling. Triage tool findings for affected versions, reachability and false positives; preserve unresolved items.
evidence: Security matrix, findings, redacted raw evidence, coverage and access limitations
pass_criteria: No unresolved release blocker; every required check executed or explicitly dispositioned; no security certification implied
cost: 60–120 min targeted; deeper assessment separately budgeted
limits: Present commission performs no scans. No model label or claimed blue/red-team method establishes testing.

title: Qualify data custody and actual restore
risk: Silent loss, false archive ACK or unusable backup
inputs: Data map, retention contract, fixture DBs/archives, supported snapshot method
method: Test commit/ACK ordering, duplicates, partial writes, interrupted sends, corruption and restart with disposable copies. Receipt must identify receiver, exact record/version and durable accepted content; mismatch never authorizes eviction. Verify pending rows retained during outage, bounded pressure/defer behavior and historical gaps visible. Restore a coherent snapshot in isolation and reconcile schema, representative records, digests, identity and app reads; measure recovery time/point.
evidence: Failure matrix, archive receipt evidence, restore log and reconciliation counts
pass_criteria: No acknowledged record/version lost or duplicated semantically; corrupt/foreign receipts rejected; restore meets declared RPO/RTO
limits: Hashes prove equality only to a trusted reference. Restore is not an in-place overwrite of the only live store.

title: Verify diagnostics privacy and optional telemetry
risk: Sensitive content leaks or invisible failure
inputs: Data contract, logging paths, export/diagnostics schema and consent design
method: Use synthetic secret/path markers to inspect allowed outputs, logs, backups, exports and intended artifacts. Redact before persistence or queueing. Require useful refusal/retry/backlog diagnostics without raw secrets. If telemetry exists, test default off, explicit consent, schema allowlist, destination, retention, queue bounds, disable and pending-report disposal. If absent, record NOT_IMPLEMENTED and remove feature claims or seek an owner launch tradeoff.
evidence: Canary tests, diagnostic samples, network observation where authorized and consent-state results
pass_criteria: No prohibited fields leave approved boundary; failures visible; telemetry consent contract met for enabled release scope
limits: No telemetry receiver was selected in the reused roadmap; this study does not establish implementation.

title: Freeze and qualify distributable artifacts
risk: Tested source differs from shipped package
inputs: Final source identity, actual allowlist/build config, final docs/version
method: Build a new candidate directory without overwriting prior evidence. Inventory every archive member, modes, symlinks, assets, licenses, generated docs and import closure; compare manifest/hashes independently. Review inclusion/exclusion and privacy limits. Test extracted bytes, not just the development tree. Record toolchain/build inputs and artifact digest; compare rebuilds if reproducibility is claimed. Align version consumers, install/update instructions, PDFs and limitations.
evidence: Source-to-artifact provenance, member list, hashes, final docs and extracted-artifact smoke
pass_criteria: Zero unexplained files or missing required files; exact candidate version coherent; qualification binds to artifact digest
limits: CodexControl mapping release/STATUS.md to root RELEASE_STATUS.md can recreate stale metadata even when root is current.

title: Review the final change and resolve findings
risk: Late fixes invalidate earlier evidence or reviewer repeats author claims
inputs: Final diff, G03 plan, check/finding register, actual artifacts
method: Read complete final diff for unintended behavior, weakened security, dropped notices and unsupported claims. When separately authorized, give one independent reviewer a fixed scope and immutable inputs; ask for disconfirming tests and findings, not a second blanket scan. Author records disagreements with evidence. No worker spawning in this research. Re-run affected checks after each accepted fix using invalidation rules, then final aggregate set.
evidence: Final diff receipt, review report or explicit independence limit, rerun map
pass_criteria: Every blocker closed with exit-test evidence or owner-approved scope change; final evidence current
cost: 20–45 min author; 30–60 min independent review if authorized
limits: A second AI opinion may help but is not a second human or Scorecard human review. Missing required independence stays visible.

title: Deliver decision packet and obtain push approval
risk: A summary implies approval or risk acceptance
inputs: Evidence register, final report, unresolved risks and immutable IDs
method: Summarize scope, source/artifact identities, results, omissions, reused evidence, risk decisions and recovery. Recommend READY_FOR_PUSH_REVIEW, READY_WITH_ACCEPTED_RISK or BLOCKED. Present exact repository/ref, old/new SHA, visibility, artifact hashes and requested action. Obtain the owner's explicit push approval if not already valid for that exact tuple. Keep publication/deploy/tag approval separate.
evidence: Filled final report, owner risk decisions and approval receipt
pass_criteria: Required gates satisfied; no unknown required work disguised as N/A; approval covers current immutable tuple
basis: S01 PO.4.2; S21; PROJECT-REVIEW; engineering judgment
limits: A research report, green suite or prior permission to work does not authorize a push.

title: Push only the approved change and verify remote
risk: Wrong target, races or unsuccessful/partial remote update
inputs: Valid G15 approval, fresh target identity and working-tree check
method: Re-read target ref/visibility and local candidate before action. If SHA or policy changed, stop and rebase/requalify through authority. Execute only the named ref update; no force, broad tags, release, deploy or visibility change unless separately explicit. After uncertain transport, read remote first before retrying. Compare remote SHA, artifact digest if applicable and required CI/check conclusions at the exact SHA and run attempt.
evidence: Remote ref readback, visibility readback and CI evidence or precise unavailable state
pass_criteria: Remote equals approved source; required CI succeeded on that SHA; unavailable/skipped/stale results never called PASS
limits: No push or live CI run is performed under this commission. CodexControl's own metadata panel is not independent qualification.

title: Close and preserve the session
risk: Lost progress, abandoned helpers or an inflated completion claim
inputs: Current work inventory, final registers and owned test processes
method: Save recovery checkpoint and next action at every session end, even on failure/denial. Update the existing canonical checkpoint when edits are authorized; do not create competing product authority. Record local-only versus off-host preservation, unfinished files, target/process ownership and evidence hashes. Stop only owned disposable helpers; retain source and evidence. Deliver actual paths despite export/upload failure.
evidence: Session closeout, preserved deliverables and next-start instructions
pass_criteria: No unresolved custody uncertainty hidden; run state accurately identifies research, candidate, approval and remote verification phases
limits: Denied action stops on its target; independent permitted work continues. Budget expiry yields honest incompleteness, never PASS.
